title: Compose agent work and durable Orbit sessions into an Eon workspace
description:
Contract routing:
- Consumes user-approved EON-C8, indexed as Planned on 2026-08-08. The first Eon topology/action owner is activated through eon-pxn.1; later owner and consumer children remain separately gated.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and consumes exact accepted Orbit and Venus contracts.
- Requires separate owner contracts for any new Orbit session discovery or observation and Venus multi-surface or agent-attention behavior. This activation changes the EON-C8 index and Beads planning only; it changes no runtime behavior.

Why:
Eon should be agent-first rather than merely agent-compatible. Its defining product opportunity is to organize durable human and agent work without moving terminal state or UI layout into Orbit. The first composition has one Orbit/Venus pair and no explicit workspace, repository/worktree, AgentRun, service, artifact, session-switching, attention, or background-task model.

Irreducible model:
- Eon Workspace groups repositories or worktrees, AgentRuns, services, artifacts, execution-target references, and mappings to independent Orbit sessions.
- AgentRun is an explicit Eon product identity. It is not a pane, PTY, process, Orbit session, provider thread, or Venus view, although it may link to those values.
- Orbit owns authoritative process and terminal-session lifetime and terminal content.
- Provider integrations, when separately approved, own provider-native semantic evidence.
- Eon owns normalized AgentRun identity, relationships, lifecycle policy, source-aware status, attention policy, and the ordered horizontal-tab and per-tab vertical-pane topology.
- Venus owns native horizontal-tab and visual accordion-pane materialization, attention presentation, focus, geometry, hit testing, and ephemeral view state.

Scope:
In scope are Eon-owned workspace and AgentRun identities; repository/worktree and session mappings; launch, resume, stop and cleanup policy; one real coding-agent workflow; a bounded native two-axis workspace with horizontal tabs and per-tab visual vertical accordion stacks; explicit tab and pane creation; direct directional traversal; source-aware attention in persistent headers; the smallest deterministic machine-readable Eon actions; one bounded declarative workspace or profile schema over those same identities and actions; and a separately proved Eon-managed interactive environment whose tool selection, private configuration, command projection, and component identities remain Eon product policy.

Out of scope are terminal-text or process-name heuristics as authoritative agent state, provider compatibility promises, arbitrary raw terminal control, Orbit-owned agent policy or layouts, a virtual or fuzzy picker for ordinary vertical pane traversal, arbitrary split trees, nested or floating terminal panes, generic popup infrastructure, a generalized widget or plugin framework, remote machines, web or mobile, machine-restart recovery, durable layout restoration, and Nova or Zellij compatibility. The managed tools remain independently owned components rather than Eon forks or compatibility surfaces.

Canonical CLI and action boundary:
- Eon owns one semantic action registry for workspace and AgentRun product state.
- The `eon` CLI is the canonical external projection for both humans and agents. Human-readable output and deterministic `--json` output consume the same actions and identities rather than forming separate APIs.
- The running Eon supervisor remains the only live workspace and action-state owner. A second CLI invocation reaches it through one private Eon-owned local control endpoint and never addresses Orbit, ORBS, ORBF, or Venus directly or reconstructs live state from files.
- Configuration, external programs, and a later MCP adapter may consume the same accepted actions. None of them becomes an authorization owner, plugin ABI, or second state owner.
design:
Implementation sequence:
1. Begin only after eon-ax4 proves the one-session composition with real agent dogfood, Orbit and Venus graduate, and orb-bi4.7 accepts this as the single next frontier.
2. EON-C8 was approved and indexed before runtime code. Activation creates only the next owner child: eon-pxn.1 owns the minimal Eon topology and actions. Create the managed-environment, Venus consumer, cross-repository dogfood, later appearance, declarative-profile, or any required Orbit child only immediately before its turn and after its exact contract routing is approved; none silently expands EON-C8.
3. Complete the Eon reference gate. Required before code: exact accepted Orbit and Venus revisions; exact current Herdr runtime, agent-state and socket/action surfaces; Amp Orbs workspace model; VS Code Agent Host client-independent execution; Canario workspace interaction; and exact Nova and Zellij workflow comparisons, including Zellij visual stacking and its alternative virtual picker behavior. Accept mechanisms only for the question they answer; neither Zellij surface is a compatibility target.
4. Keep an AgentRun independent from its representations. A workspace may contain ordinary non-agent sessions. An AgentRun may link to a provider thread, one or more Orbit sessions, services and artifacts. A Venus tab or pane only materializes a session and never becomes the session or AgentRun identity.
5. Separate three kinds of state:
   - execution state from the authoritative process or Orbit lifecycle;
   - semantic agent state from an explicit provider integration, or unknown;
   - attention state computed by Eon from explicit fresh evidence.
   Every semantic value carries its source and freshness. Never silently promote scraped output, process names, elapsed time, or titles into provider truth.
6. Prefer one Orbit process and socket per session until measurements justify a separately approved multi-session Orbit process.
7. Prove the registry together with one fixed two-axis materialization. Eon orders horizontal tabs and the vertical pane stack inside each tab. Venus shows that stack as a visual accordion: one focused pane expands, collapsed pane headers remain visible within a bounded scrollable header region, and only the focused terminal presentation is actively materialized. Directional workspace commands traverse tabs left or right and pane headers up or down; the stack itself scrolls to keep focus visible. Ordinary traversal requires no picker, palette, modal list, or fuzzy search. Every independent Orbit session continues while unfocused, collapsed, on another tab, or while Venus is absent.
8. Prove one Eon-owned semantic action registry and its canonical `eon` CLI projection. The running Eon supervisor is the only live workspace and action-state owner. A second CLI invocation uses one private Eon-owned local control endpoint; it never addresses Orbit, ORBS, ORBF, or Venus directly or reconstructs live state from files. The first actions cover status and list, create tab, create pane, focus by stable identity or direction, attach, start, wait, explicit stop, and removal of a view separately from stopping its session. Contextual action discovery reports stable action identities, typed arguments, current targets, structured results, cancellation, bounded errors, and owner-authored reasons an action is unavailable. Human-readable output and deterministic `--json` output are projections of the same registry. Structured mode emits data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, stable symbolic error codes, and no prompts when stdout is not a terminal. Preserve the accepted meaning of the existing `eon run` command rather than overloading it with AgentRun semantics. Bounded terminal observation remains absent until orb-p92 is accepted. A general event stream remains deferred until one workflow needs more than bounded `wait`. Configuration, external programs, and a later MCP adapter may consume accepted actions but do not become a plugin ABI or authorization owner.
9. Define explicit capabilities and user consent. Read-only observation and mutating actions remain separate. Raw keystroke injection, provider-specific approval, arbitrary shell execution, remote access, and secret access require separate decisions.
10. Venus consumes Eon-authored tab, pane, AgentRun and attention state through a separately approved contract. Its first native workspace surface is the horizontal tab strip and visual vertical accordion stack. Persistent tab and pane headers identify ordinary sessions and linked AgentRuns, expose only bounded source-aware attention, and provide deterministic pointer and accessible focus. This is not a sidebar, picker, popup, arbitrary layout framework, or third-party widget API. A focused-terminal mode may hide and restore workspace chrome without stopping, detaching, or changing an AgentRun or Orbit session.
11. Define tab and pane creation, focus, collapse, expansion, removal, attach, detach, workspace-chrome hide and restore, agent or process exit, Venus crash, Orbit crash, stale endpoint, explicit shutdown, cancellation, and abandoned-resource cleanup with strict bounds. Removing a view and stopping its Orbit session or AgentRun remain distinct explicit transitions.
12. Keep collapsed headers to bounded owner-authored metadata and do not continuously render inactive sessions. Add previews only after dogfood proves that headers are insufficient.

Chosen workspace shape:
- Tabs are the visible horizontal axis; each tab contains one ordered visual vertical accordion pane stack.
- Each pane maps to one independent Orbit session. Exactly one pane in the active tab is expanded; collapsed headers remain visible within bounded scrolling and do not render terminal previews.
- Directional workspace commands move left or right between tabs and up or down through the visible stack. Pointer and accessibility actions target the same ordered identities. No picker is required for vertical pane traversal.
- Tab and pane headers may display only bounded owner-authored identity, lifecycle and source-aware attention metadata. They never scrape terminal text or guess provider state.
- A hidden or unfocused pane preserves its Eon-managed lifecycle while Venus owns geometry, z-order and ephemeral focus.
- A declarative Eon workspace or profile may request this topology and its launch inputs; Eon remains topology owner, Orbit remains session owner, and Venus only materializes accepted views.
- Working-directory and environment discovery remain with the launched shell or tool, including Direnv when selected. Eon passes explicit launch inputs and does not snapshot, reinterpret, or become a second owner of the resolved environment.

Configuration boundary:
- Eon owns one versioned declarative workspace or profile schema over the same stable identities and semantic actions exposed by the CLI. Ratconfig may edit that Eon-owned schema but does not own its meaning or apply policy.
- The first schema may describe the accepted tab and pane topology, launch inputs, keybindings, and named action sequences. Applying it routes through the same action owner and cannot address Orbit or Venus protocols directly.
- Validation and apply failures are deterministic and leave prior accepted state intact. The schema has no loops, mutable variables, asynchronous callbacks, arbitrary code, custom widget trees, raw terminal control, ambient environment capture, or second workspace state owner.
- The configuration proof is a separately activated Eon child when this epic starts; planning it here creates no schema or compatibility promise.

Deferred pressure test:
- Simultaneously expanded panes, arbitrary horizontal or vertical splits, nested layout trees, floating terminal popups, drag-and-drop reordering, virtual pane pickers and durable layout restoration remain outside the first workspace slice.
- Fixed status items consume bounded owner-authored metadata and never scrape terminal text.
- Graphics remain an independent Orbit-to-Venus resource plane.
- A local execution target can later become remote or isolated without treating a host path, pane or Nix store path as global AgentRun identity.

Stop if the slice duplicates terminal, provider, protocol, layout or agent-state ownership; if child contracts are speculative; if authorization has no owner; if background cleanup cannot be bounded; if ordinary vertical traversal requires a picker, popup or generic layout framework; or if a published compatibility surface is required before this single workflow proves value.

Accepted managed interactive environment:
- After the minimal topology and action owner, a separate Eon child owns the initial interactive environment. Eon owns component selection and exact versions, launch policy, the existing private configuration root, stable managed command names, the Eon-session PATH projection, and component identity reporting. Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit continue to own their native behavior and schemas. Orbit launches exact argv and retains PTY authority; Venus owns no shell or tool policy.
- The initial set is Nushell as the default shell through `eon-nu`; Starship using native modules with only a sparse Eon override, a violet `∴ ` prompt marker, and no extra blank line; Zoxide initialization; Helix through `eon-hx`; Yazi through `eon-yazi` and `eon-ya`; and LazyGit through `eon-lazygit` with `eon-lg` as a convenience command. The long-term Eon-native editor remains separately routed through eon-ofb; managed Helix creates no permanent editor-compatibility promise.
- Outside an Eon session, only the stable `eon-*` managed commands are exposed. Inside an Eon session, an Eon-private PATH projects `nu`, `hx`, `yazi`, `ya`, and `lazygit` to the same managed executables through shims or symlinks so subprocesses and agents see the same behavior; managed Nushell supplies `lg`. Do not implement these process-visible names as shell aliases.
- Prefix only commands whose executable behavior or private configuration Eon manages. Do not add ornamental `eon-git`, `eon-starship`, or `eon-zoxide` commands. Preserve explicit child-command selection through `eon run -- COMMAND...` as the escape hatch.
- Do not add an alias-mode setting in the first slice. If real command collisions justify one, the later declarative-profile child may add one simple `tools.unprefixed = false` policy while retaining the same wrappers and private configuration. Direnv and Mise remain user-selected integrations rather than automatic Eon environment mutation.
- The canonical component manifest and `eon versions` report the same exact identities used by the Nix composition. Later direct-distribution and Home Manager paths consume that manifest and these defaults; they do not redefine them.

title: Own the minimal Eon workspace topology and semantic actions
description:
Contract routing:
- Changes and may partially prove EON-C8 only. EON-C8 is user-approved and indexed as Planned before implementation.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and the existing meanings of eon run, eon attach, versions, and config-path.
- Consumes independent Orbit session identities and accepted lifecycle behavior without changing ORBS, ORBF, Orbit, or Venus. Any missing child contract stops this Bead and returns to the owning repository.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
The consumer is one local Eon user through the canonical eon action projection and, later, a separately approved Venus adapter. Creating or focusing a tab or pane, or traversing left, right, up, or down, changes one Eon-owned live topology of stable tab and pane identities. Tabs are horizontally ordered; every tab has an ordered vertical pane stack; each pane maps explicitly to one independent Orbit session identity; Eon retains one selected pane per non-empty tab and one active tab. Venus will later render the selected pane in the active tab as the only expanded accordion pane. Unknown or stale identities, missing sessions, invalid transitions, unavailable directions, supervisor loss, and malformed actions return bounded explicit failures and leave the last accepted topology unchanged.

Current gap:
The accepted alpha supervises one Orbit socket and one Venus client. It has no Eon-owned workspace topology, stable tab or pane identity, multi-session mapping, semantic workspace action owner, or live control endpoint. Venus must not invent those values.

Prerequisites:
- eon-ax4 is closed with the accepted Nix-only Linux alpha.
- orb-bi4.7 is closed and selects eon-pxn as the sole post-graduation frontier.
- EON-C8 is approved and indexed.
- At the execution baseline, record the exact accepted Eon HEAD, affected EON-C8 state, Orbit ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 proof revision, current pinned Orbit artifact, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and active session identity. Stop if the accepted Orbit artifact cannot supply independent endpoints without a new Orbit contract.

Ownership:
- Eon owns stable opaque workspace, tab, and pane identities; ordering; active and selected identities; explicit pane-to-Orbit-session mappings; semantic workspace actions; and the private local control boundary.
- The running Eon supervisor is the sole live topology and action-state owner. CLI invocations and the later Venus adapter consume that owner rather than rebuilding state from files.
- Orbit remains the sole owner of every process, PTY, terminal state, retained history, attachment, and session lifetime.
- Venus remains the future owner of native geometry, focus, rendering, accessibility, hit testing, and accordion materialization.

First slice:
Implement only the state and actions needed to inspect the topology, create tabs and panes, focus a stable identity, and traverse tabs left or right and pane selections up or down. Human-readable CLI output and deterministic --json output must project the same action results. A direction with no target is explicitly unavailable and does not wrap or mutate state. Keep one Orbit process and endpoint per pane unless measured evidence and a separately approved Orbit decision justify consolidation.

Scope boundary:
No Venus UI, managed Nushell or tool defaults, AgentRun or provider model, attention inference, terminal observation, arbitrary split tree, picker, simultaneous expanded panes, drag-and-drop, durable layout restoration, declarative profile, event stream, MCP, plugins, remote access, isolated execution, appearance effects, new public protocol, or compatibility promise. View removal and session stop remain separate later actions; this child must not conflate them.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: this Bead and comments; AGENTS.md; docs/CONTRACTS.md EON-C8; current Eon launcher and tests; exact accepted Orbit ORB-C1 and ORB-C3 contracts and proof; exact current Herdr workspace, supervisor, and socket/action surfaces; Amp Orbs workspace identity model; VS Code Agent Host client-independent execution; Canario frontend and SessionStore at Rio 3e41b8b19a1c; exact current Zellij tab and stacked-pane action mechanisms; and exact Nova 37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c only for workflow comparison.
- Comparison only: Helheim live-modifiable Emacs architecture and broader extension model. It does not change Eon ownership or justify an embedded language.
- Conditional on a named failure: current Venus source and protocol only if the opaque consumer handoff cannot be specified from accepted contracts; other Orbit source only if independent session endpoints are insufficient.
- Rejected scope: copying reference code, adopting a reference protocol or compatibility target, provider semantics, general plugins, arbitrary layouts, or moving PTY or rendering ownership into Eon.

Minimum code shape:
1. Reuse the existing Rust product binary and supervisor boundary. Prefer a small Eon-owned topology model and direct action dispatcher; add no framework or runtime dependency unless the crate gate proves a complete responsibility.
2. Give the topology model stable opaque identities, explicit order, active-tab selection, per-tab pane selection, and opaque Orbit endpoint mappings. Store no terminal frame, text, PTY state, provider state, or Venus geometry.
3. Route the canonical CLI and future adapters through the same action owner. The private local control transport is an implementation seam, not a public plugin ABI.
4. Prove deterministic state transitions first, then prove one live supervisor with two tabs, three substitute Orbit endpoints, and a second CLI invocation. Do not require Venus for this owner proof.
5. Keep process, path, and socket code behind the existing Unix boundary and record neutral or isolated-platform-dependency disposition. Stop for a macOS blocker instead of creating a speculative platform framework.

First meaningful check:
A deterministic transition test starts from an empty owner state, creates two tabs and three panes mapped to three distinct opaque session identities, focuses by identity and left/right/up/down direction, and proves stable order, one selected pane per non-empty tab, explicit boundary failures, and no mutation after rejected actions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The execution baseline and Reference gate are recorded before production, test, manifest, or generated-fixture edits, including exact source identities, licenses, adopted mechanisms, rejected scope, ownership consequences, platform disposition, and the first check.
2. One Eon-owned model holds stable opaque tab and pane identities, horizontal tab order, vertical per-tab pane order, active tab, one selected pane per non-empty tab, and explicit mappings to distinct Orbit session identities. It stores no terminal, PTY, presentation, provider, or Venus state.
3. One semantic action owner supports bounded topology inspection, tab creation, pane creation, stable-identity focus, left/right tab traversal, and up/down pane traversal. The CLI human view and deterministic --json view consume the same results.
4. Left/right and up/down select the intended stable identity. A missing target, unknown or stale identity, duplicate request, invalid transition, malformed action, unavailable supervisor, or missing session yields a bounded explicit error and leaves the last accepted topology unchanged.
5. The running supervisor is the sole live topology and action-state owner. A second eon invocation reaches it through one private Eon control boundary; it does not read live topology from files or speak ORBS, ORBF, or Venus protocols directly.
6. The proof uses at least two tabs and three independent substitute or accepted Orbit session endpoints. Useful child work survives focus and tab changes and control-client loss. The child introduces no multi-session Orbit daemon assumption.
7. Existing eon run, eon attach, versions, config-path, EON-C1 through EON-C4 behavior, manifest identity, private runtime-directory validation, and accepted partial-failure semantics remain green.
8. Focus changes never stop, detach, replace, or reinterpret an Orbit session. View removal and session termination are not added or conflated.
9. Strong tests cover the deterministic transition boundary and one process-level action path. Run cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, the cheapest relevant Nix composition check, and git diff --check.
10. No new dependency, public protocol, schema, Venus surface, managed tool default, AgentRun/provider state, observation capability, arbitrary layout, picker, persistence promise, plugin/MCP surface, isolation target, remote behavior, or appearance effect is introduced.
11. Closure updates EON-C8 with the exact proof revision and honest status, records limitations and cross-repository handoff requirements, reconciles the parent Bead and dependency graph, updates current documentation and README LOC accounting, and does not claim full native workspace proof before the separate Venus and dogfood children pass.
notes: Implemented and mechanically proved the minimal Eon-owned live topology/action slice at 1a00a9f6de171e944c3c31a9f72ee2cc92d8fa15; documentation proof is 0d25711ef5fb12cbc1576cf9800c7931a67ba432. Five fresh-eyes passes removed 22 net Rust lines and corrected bounded control scheduling, timeout failure handling, socket ownership and cleanup, test cleanup and readiness ordering, active-tab missing-session validation, impossible-status handling, and initial-session documentation. Proof asserts mode 0600 only after a completed control round trip, ordinary cleanup at supervisor exit, and preservation of a replacement socket. EON-C8 is Partially proved pending the separately approved Venus consumer and composed native dogfood. No dependency, manifest, child protocol, defaults, provider, plugin, persistence, remote, or appearance scope was added.

Third-pass failing proof — root cause

Command: cargo test --locked -p eon --test workspace_control
Result: failed at the new post-supervisor assertion because runtime/eon.sock still existed after a successful supervisor exit.

Root cause
- create_control_listener records the full SocketIdentity before fs::set_permissions.
- SocketIdentity includes ctime and ctime_nsec so Orbit startup can distinguish a replaced endpoint.
- chmod to 0600 changes the control socket ctime. ControlSocketGuard later compares the pre-chmod full identity, concludes the path was replaced, and deliberately skips removal.
- This regression was introduced when the first fresh-eyes pass moved guard creation before chmod to cover setup failures.

Minimum fix / proof card
- ControlSocketGuard needs only dev+inode identity, not Orbit startup timestamp identity. The open UnixListener retains the inode until after the guard drops, so a replacement path cannot legitimately share that identity while this owner exists; chmod may change ctime without changing ownership.
- Keep full dev+inode+ctime identity in socket_identity and wait_for_socket so Orbit endpoint replacement detection is unchanged.
- Keep the guard before chmod so permission or nonblocking setup failure still cleans its own socket.
- Production behavior changes only from stale control-path leakage to correct identity-checked removal. Permissions, public outputs, wire, process lifecycle, Orbit checks, and all other behavior remain unchanged.
- The strengthened existing process test is the first check: 0600 while live and absent after the successful supervisor exit.

title: Prove the Eon-managed interactive environment
description:
Contract routing:
- Follows the completed eon-pxn.1 topology and action owner. This child changes no runtime behavior until its managed-environment contract is approved and indexed.
- Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and the partial EON-C8 topology proof. It may extend the canonical component graph and composed launch policy only through an explicitly approved Eon contract and exact child identities.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
A local Eon user starts the default interactive Session, invokes an Eon-managed command outside Eon, or launches a subprocess inside an Eon Session. Eon selects one exact managed interactive environment: Nushell, sparse Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit. Outside Eon, stable eon-prefixed commands expose managed executables without shadowing the user toolchain. Inside Eon, one Eon-private PATH projects the accepted unprefixed executable names to the same artifacts, and managed Nushell supplies lg. Missing artifacts, invalid private configuration, manifest mismatch, or launch failure returns an explicit bounded error and never mutates global user configuration or PATH.

Ownership:
- Eon owns component selection and exact versions, launch policy, the existing private configuration root, stable managed command names, the Eon-session PATH projection, and component identity reporting.
- Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit retain their native behavior and configuration schemas.
- Orbit launches exact argv and retains process, PTY, terminal state, and Session authority. Venus owns no shell or tool policy.

Accepted first slice:
- Nushell is the default Eon shell through eon-nu.
- Starship uses native modules plus one sparse Eon override, a violet ∴ prompt marker, and no extra blank line.
- Zoxide initialization is enabled in managed Nushell.
- Stable external commands are eon-nu, eon-hx, eon-yazi, eon-ya, eon-lazygit, and eon-lg.
- Inside an Eon Session, an Eon-private PATH exposes nu, hx, yazi, ya, and lazygit as process-visible names backed by the same managed artifacts. Managed Nushell supplies lg.
- eon run -- COMMAND... remains the explicit escape hatch and retains its accepted semantics.

Scope boundary:
No global aliases or PATH mutation, first-slice alias-mode setting, ornamental eon-git/eon-starship/eon-zoxide commands, copied child schemas, child forks, Carapace, automatic Direnv or Mise activation, arbitrary shell framework, plugin/MCP surface, declarative profile, direct bundle, Home Manager module, remote behavior, or editor replacement. The eon-ofb decision continues to own any later Eon-native editor.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: AGENTS.md; this Bead and parent decisions; current Eon manifest, flake, wrappers, launcher, configuration path, eon versions, and runtime tests; exact Nova revision 37f36efcabf16c41d03e182917926e7b8e56139c for isolated native configuration, managed wrappers, and prompt/tool composition only; primary documentation and exact selected releases for Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit; their licenses; and current Nixpkgs package composition.
- Conditional: current Orbit launch contract if exact default argv cannot be supplied by its accepted interface; macOS package evidence if a selected tool or path projection reveals a concrete blocker.
- Comparison only: user shell frameworks, Direnv, Mise, and Carapace. They do not enter the first slice.
- Rejected: copying Nova configuration or schemas, compatibility with Nova, global command shadowing, shell aliases as the process-visible projection, a second component graph, or moving tool behavior into Eon.

Minimum code shape:
1. Approve and index the smallest managed-environment Eon contract before production or manifest edits.
2. Run one dependency gate covering exact versions, licenses, direct/transitive/native/Nix closure cost, overlap with the existing closure, upgrade burden, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, and replacement cost. Stop for approval before manifest changes.
3. Extend the canonical component manifest once; Nix and eon versions consume that same graph. Add no second version table.
4. Reuse the existing Eon configuration root and propagate that exact root into Sessions as EON_CONFIG_HOME while retaining XDG_CONFIG_HOME for child configuration. This prevents nested managed dispatch from resolving an eon/eon path. Store only sparse Eon-owned overrides and native child configuration; do not translate or mirror whole child schemas.
5. Install stable eon-prefixed wrapper or symlink names outside Eon. Build one private bin directory for Eon Sessions whose unprefixed names target those same artifacts. Do not mutate the ambient user PATH.
6. Route the default no-command Session to the accepted eon-nu executable through the existing Eon-to-Orbit launch boundary. Preserve eon run -- COMMAND... byte-for-byte and semantically.
7. Prove artifacts and behavior, not configuration literals: executable resolution outside and inside Eon, exact identity reporting, isolated config paths, shell startup, prompt behavior, zoxide initialization, managed lg, subprocess lookup, explicit-command escape, and absence of global shadowing.

Platform disposition:
The selection policy and command semantics are neutral. The current canonical manifest target, Nix composition, and Unix PATH/symlink/exec projection are x86_64-linux isolated platform dependencies. A macOS channel will require one accepted target-capable manifest representation plus bundle-relative artifact injection and link creation; this must preserve the same component graph rather than introduce a second version owner. Any newly discovered tool or wrapper assumption that blocks a native signed macOS bundle must name the exact replacement shape and removal cost before acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Before implementation, the user-visible managed-environment contract is approved and indexed; the execution baseline records HEAD, AGENTS hash, affected EON contracts, exact component proofs, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and active identity.
2. The reference gate records exact source identities, licenses, adopted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, ownership consequences, platform disposition, and the first meaningful check.
3. The dependency gate records exact versions, maintenance and API status, direct/transitive/native/Nix cost, closure overlap and marginal size, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, upgrade burden, and replacement cost; manifest edits wait for explicit approval.
4. The canonical manifest is the sole component identity graph for Nushell, Starship, Zoxide, Helix, Yazi, and LazyGit, eon versions reports the exact accepted identities used by the composition, and the composed package retains their exact upstream license notices.
5. The default no-command Eon Session launches managed Nushell through eon-nu. eon run -- COMMAND... preserves its accepted explicit-command behavior.
6. Outside Eon, the package exposes only eon-nu, eon-hx, eon-yazi, eon-ya, eon-lazygit, and eon-lg for the managed set and does not shadow nu, hx, yazi, ya, lazygit, or unrelated user commands.
7. Inside an Eon Session, one Eon-private PATH projects nu, hx, yazi, ya, and lazygit to the same managed artifacts. The projection is process-visible to subprocesses and agents, not implemented only as shell aliases. Managed Nushell supplies lg.
8. Managed Nushell uses the existing private Eon configuration root. Starship uses native modules with only a sparse Eon override, a violet ∴ marker, and no extra blank line. Zoxide initialization works without Eon owning either native schema.
9. Missing tools, invalid private configuration, manifest mismatch, and launch failure produce bounded explicit failures and do not modify global user configuration or shell startup files, environment, aliases, or PATH.
10. Strong artifact-level and process-level checks prove external prefixed resolution, internal unprefixed resolution, exact version reporting, isolated native configuration, default shell startup, prompt shape, Zoxide initialization, LazyGit lg behavior, subprocess lookup, same-root nested managed dispatch, and the explicit-command escape.
11. No new public protocol, child fork, compatibility promise, alias-mode setting, ornamental wrapper, Carapace, automatic Direnv or Mise activation, plugin/MCP surface, declarative profile, direct distribution, Home Manager behavior, remote behavior, or Eon-native editor enters the slice.
12. Closure reconciles the parent sequence and records exact proof revisions, checks, LOC, closure measurements, known Linux limits, macOS replacement cost, and the next separately approved Venus tabs/accordion consumer. It does not claim EON-C8 fully proved.

Dependency gate — EON-C9 / eon-pxn.2 — approval required before manifest edits

Capability and selected ownership
- Capability: one reproducible interactive shell, prompt, directory jumper, editor, file manager, and Git TUI selected by Eon and reachable through bounded command projection. Reimplementing any child capability is rejected; the selected upstream executable remains its owner.
- Selection: reuse the exact packages from pinned Nixpkgs 567a49d1913ce81ac6e9582e3553dd90a955875f and the already pinned Helix/Yazi artifacts. Exact candidates and maintenance status as of 2026-08-08
- Nushell 0.113.1, commit 7b7df4aa68e957cf38b9d8157c35fa7523f44a6d, MIT, official release 2026-05-30. Latest upstream is 0.114.1 from 2026-07-11.

- The pinned versions are deliberately selected over newer one-off overrides: they are recent, packaged and checked together by one locked Nixpkgs revision, and provide every relied-on CLI. Upgrade on a deliberate Nixpkgs rotation or a demonstrated security, compatibility, or required-feature need.

Measured Linux x86_64 runtime cost
- Baseline Eon artifact: /nix/store/13rpbajlpqskc66kz4jiqcw68pv18yxy-eon-0.1.0, NAR 3,041,512 bytes, closure 1,457,951,088 bytes across 368 store paths.
- Combined candidate set: standalone closure 159,943,232 bytes. Baseline plus all four is 1,561,147,112 bytes across 376 paths: marginal 103,196,024 bytes, approximately 98.4 MiB or 7.08 percent. Existing closure overlap is 56,747,208 bytes, approximately 54.1 MiB.
- Nushell: 109,133,104-byte standalone closure over 7 paths; 60,887,376-byte marginal increase and 1 new path over Eon. Installed binary NAR contribution is 60,887,376 bytes.
- Starship: 61,795,080-byte standalone closure over 7 paths; 13,549,352-byte marginal increase and 1 new path. Installed output NAR is 13,549,352 bytes.
- Zoxide: 63,703,872-byte standalone closure over 14 paths; 7,076,024-byte marginal increase and 4 new paths. Its output is 1,294,592 bytes; the remaining marginal cost is chiefly the Nixpkgs-patched fzf runtime.
- LazyGit: 62,246,104-byte standalone closure over 8 paths; 22,244,104-byte marginal increase and 2 new paths. Its output is 21,672,936 bytes; remaining runtime data includes mailcap and shared timezone/iana data.

Direct, transitive, native, and build cost
- Nushell and Starship runtime outputs directly reference only glibc and GCC runtime already present in Eon. Nushell is a Rust build using pkg-config and Linux Python with zstd/libX11 build inputs; Starship is a Rust build with generated shell completions.
- Zoxide is a Rust build whose Nixpkgs expression pins fzf into its generated behavior; its runtime closure adds zoxide, fzf, and their small dependencies. LazyGit is a Go module build with vendored dependencies and small runtime data references.
- Nix substitutes supplied every selected executable in this environment. Source rebuild replacement remains reproducible from the pinned Nixpkgs derivations and fixed Cargo or Go dependency hashes.
- Expected Eon-owned implementation is one small Rust dispatch/exec path, one Nix private-bin/wrapper composition, and sparse native configuration, estimated at 80 to 140 handwritten production lines before tests and documentation. Exact LOC is measured at closure. No duplicate version table or configuration-schema implementation is introduced.

Behavior, portability, upgrade, and replacement
- Real artifacts reported the selected versions. Nushell exposes stable --config and --env-config startup paths; Starship 1.25.1 generated valid Nushell initialization; Zoxide 0.9.9 generated valid Nushell 0.89+ initialization; Nixpkgs itself carries a Nushell/Zoxide integration test; LazyGit exposes direct config-dir/file options but needs no Eon override in this slice.
- Nix package metadata and upstream distributions support x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin for all four. PATH, symlink, and exec behavior is available on macOS. The isolated Nix composition is not a macOS distribution proof; a native bundle later replaces store paths and makeWrapper scripts with bundle-relative paths and the same private links. Estimated replacement is one packaging adapter and artifact test, at most roughly 100 lines, with no contract, manifest, Rust policy, or user-data migration.
- Upgrades change one manifest identity plus the pinned package expression/hash evidence, regenerate native init files, and rerun the same artifact checks. Command reliance is deliberately narrow; removal cost is deleting four manifest components, their Nix bindings/config generation, wrapper links, and the default-shell selection. No global state or migration remains.

Alternatives rejected
- No dependency fails the selected product contract. Ambient host executables lose exact identity and reproducibility. Reimplementing a shell, prompt, jumper, editor, file manager, or Git TUI duplicates mature owners. Latest one-off overrides add four update tracks and unshared build hashes for no required capability. Four flake inputs duplicate resolution nodes when manifest revisions plus existing Nixpkgs hashes already reproduce the exact source. Nova-style layered configuration and shell frameworks add schema, merging, and migration ownership outside this slice.

Approval boundary
- Recommended decision: accept the six-component managed environment with the four new pinned Nixpkgs artifacts and 103,196,024-byte marginal closure cost. No component-manifest, runtime, test, or Nix composition edit has been made yet. Explicit user approval is required before those edits.

title: Expose a versioned Eon workspace snapshot/action boundary to Venus
description:
Contract routing:
- Implements the missing Eon producer prerequisite for the approved Venus materialization bead ven-c87.
- Extends the approved EON-C8 workspace owner with one versioned consumer boundary. Preserves EON-C1 through EON-C4 and EON-C9.
- Adds EON-C10 under the user's explicit direction to fix the named versioned Eon workspace snapshot/action prerequisite.

Consumer, trigger, result, failures:
Venus or the canonical Eon CLI connects to the explicit local Eon workspace endpoint and submits a versioned inspect or existing semantic workspace action. The running Eon supervisor validates the request, remains the sole live owner, and returns one complete accepted workspace snapshot containing stable ordered tab, pane, and session identities, active and selected identities, liveness, and exact Orbit endpoint mappings. Version mismatch, malformed or oversized input, unavailable action, unknown identity, unrepresentable state, or supervisor absence returns a bounded structured failure without partial state mutation.

Ownership:
- Eon owns EONW v1, its codec, action vocabulary, workspace topology and mappings, acceptance, and complete snapshot.
- The running Eon supervisor remains the sole live state and action owner.
- The CLI and Venus are consumers; neither mirrors the schema or reconstructs state.
- Orbit remains the sole PTY, process, terminal-state, and session authority.
- Venus later owns native materialization, geometry, focus, accessibility, and semantic event emission.

Scope and update order:
This issue publishes the Eon producer boundary by reusing the existing private local control endpoint and Workspace::dispatch owner. The exact current Venus revision accepts only one Orbit socket and cannot truthfully declare or receive EONW. Therefore the canonical consumer requirement and second launch input belong after an exact Venus consumer revision exists: Eon producer proof, then ven-c87 consumption, then Eon composition integration. No event stream, general plugin or MCP API, remote access, authorization framework, durable layout storage, AgentRun model, raw terminal data, Venus implementation, or compatibility window.
design:
Reference classification before code:
- Required: AGENTS.md; this Bead and ven-c87 blocker evidence; EON-C8 owner and tests at 1a00a9f6de171e944c3c31a9f72ee2cc92d8fa15; current control/supervisor flow; canonical manifest and validator; exact accepted Orbit ORBS v2 codec proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757 and manifest source 00b136318bea13e3f08d490468f069de6f6b9bd2; exact Venus launch boundary 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832.
- Comparison only: exact Canario/Rio reference 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 and the locally inspected Helheim project. They inform workspace UX, not protocol code shape.
- Rejected: exposing handwritten CLI JSON as the cross-repository schema, making Venus speak the private tab-delimited format, duplicating protocol types in Venus, changing the declared requirements or argv of an exact Venus revision that does not consume EONW, or moving topology/session authority.

Minimum code shape:
1. Index EON-C10 before implementation.
2. Add one dependency-free Eon-owned EONW v1 crate with bounded binary request/response framing, semantic actions, complete snapshots, and structured failures. Use the accepted ORBS fixed-header mechanism independently; copy no Orbit implementation.
3. Route the CLI and later Venus through the same EONW codec and existing Workspace::dispatch owner. Keep human and JSON CLI output as projections outside the protocol.
4. Reuse eon.sock and one request per connection. Every success returns a complete snapshot; a client may inspect again when it needs current state. No subscription or event stream.
5. Prove codec boundaries, action/snapshot round trips, CLI preservation, and real supervisor behavior with the fewest strong checks.
6. After an exact producer proof exists, register the Eon provider revision. After ven-c87 produces an exact consumer revision, separately wire the canonical requirement and explicit launch input; never predict those revisions.

Platform classification: isolated Unix local-socket dependency. EONW values are platform-neutral bytes and identities; Eon and Venus own their narrow Unix path conversion. A macOS client can consume the same bounded byte protocol over a local Unix-domain socket.
acceptance_criteria:
1. EON-C10 is approved and indexed with consumer, trigger, complete result, bounded failures, one owner, and honest candidate/proof status.
2. One dependency-free Eon-owned EONW v1 crate represents complete workspace snapshots and the existing bounded actions without copying Orbit schemas or exposing raw terminal state.
3. The supervisor accepts only EONW v1, bounds all input, rejects malformed requests deterministically, and applies mutations only through Workspace::dispatch.
4. Every successful inspect or accepted action returns a complete snapshot with ordered stable tab/pane/session IDs, active/selected identities, liveness, and exact Orbit endpoint bytes. Failed actions preserve prior state.
5. The canonical CLI uses the same EONW request/response codec while preserving current human and JSON behavior.
6. Focused tests prove fixed framing, version mismatch, malformed/oversized input, every action round trip, complete snapshot round trip and invariants, structured owner failures, and existing real workspace control.
7. The current canonical Venus identity, requirements, and one-socket launch plan remain unchanged because revision 2d36c72dc87ca5416e22d6afdc35c6ab4e2fb832 does not consume EONW. The Bead records the exact producer-to-consumer-to-composition update order.
8. No event stream, general plugin surface, remote transport, authorization framework, AgentRun state, durable restoration, raw terminal content, or Venus rendering is added.
9. README, architecture/contracts documentation, CHANGELOG for the consumer-visible protocol, and the handwritten LOC scorecard describe the exact implemented boundary while preserving concurrent icon work.
10. Required Rust checks, existing canonical manifest validation, and git diff --check pass. Proof and graph registration wait for an exact committed producer revision; consumer requirement and launch wiring wait for an exact committed Venus revision.
close_reason: Proved EON-C10 at exact revision 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d; the versioned Eon workspace producer boundary is complete and ready for ven-c87 consumption.

- Current tab-delimited control bytes are unversioned and mix presentation mode with actions; Venus must not learn them.

- New source-of-truth owner: one eon-workspace-protocol crate for EONW v1 values and codec.

Cheapest first meaningful check:
A dependency-free protocol unit test that round-trips every action and one complete snapshot and rejects a changed version, malformed shape, and trailing bytes. It must fail before the codec exists.

Exit condition:
Stop if the shared crate cannot remain the only protocol-schema owner, if exact endpoint mapping cannot be represented within the bounded frame, if mutation bypasses Workspace::dispatch, if a new dependency becomes necessary, or if the current Venus revision would need to be misrepresented.

title: Integrate the proved Venus workspace client
description:
## Contract

Preserve EON-C1 through EON-C4, EON-C9, and EON-C10 while completing the accepted EON-C8 composition slice: Eon launches exact Venus consumer proof `932be5ce68a42b72e8b0bf5953c74f7a8af51f1e` with both the initial Orbit endpoint and Eon-owned EONW v1 workspace endpoint, so native tabs and panes follow the live workspace. No new product contract.

## Scope

Update the canonical component graph and Nix pin, reuse the existing Venus argv interface in supervisor and attach paths, align current-state docs and generated agent policy, verify the composed runtime, commit, and refresh the active Nix profile. Preserve all child-repository dirty paths.

## References and dependencies

Consume Venus `932be5ce68a42b72e8b0bf5953c74f7a8af51f1e`, EONW v1 producer proof `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`, and Orbit source `00b136318bea13e3f08d490468f069de6f6b9bd2` with ORBF v1 / ORBS v2 proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`. No new dependency.

The manifest validates, Venus receives `orbit.sock` and `eon.sock` in both launch paths, the locked Rust suite and Nix build pass, a fresh isolated composed runtime exposes workspace-aware Venus, agent policy requires stale Orbit/Venus warnings, the active profile resolves to the committed package, and live user Sessions are not stopped.

title: Clarify Eon public and technical naming
description:
Contract:
No EON runtime contract changes. This decision controls names in Eon documentation and planning metadata.

Prerequisites:
- The user selected Yazelix Eon as the product-line name.
- Eon owns the cross-project composition language while Orbit and Venus keep their technical ownership.

Reference gate:
- Directional collision research: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@demgun/eon, https://www.eon.io/, and https://orbit.build/ show that short Eon and Orbit names already exist in adjacent software markets.
- Treat this evidence as a reason to lead with Yazelix Eon and to perform package, command, domain, and trademark clearance before public release; it is not legal clearance.

Decision:
- Public product: Yazelix Eon, shortened to Eon after first mention.
- Platform labels, only after those surfaces exist: Eon for desktop, Eon for mobile, and Eon for the web.
- User-facing capability: Sessions.
- Technical roles: the Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime. Role words remain lowercase descriptors, not three public product names.
- Promote a component name publicly only if users can independently install, choose, configure, or use that component.

Acceptance checks:
- README distinguishes public names, future platform labels, user-facing capabilities, and technical roles without implying unimplemented surfaces exist.
- Architecture documentation records the same naming boundary and uses semantic role labels in the composition diagram.
- Contract IDs and ownership remain unchanged.
- README LOC scorecard, Markdown paths, Beads state, and git diff checks pass.

Scope boundary:
Documentation and mutable Eon planning metadata only. No runtime, command, repository, package, domain, contract, proof-state, child-repository, or historical Bead-ID rename is included.
close_reason: Documented the approved hybrid naming model in README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Yazelix Eon is the public product, Sessions is the user-facing capability, and Eon orchestrator, Venus client, and Orbit session runtime are technical role descriptions. Future platform labels remain conditional. No runtime contract, command, repository, package, child-project, or historical ID changed. Verified Bead lint, Markdown paths, EON-C identifiers, absence of live Astra wording, the 611-line LOC scorecard, and git diff checks.
